judgment.invariant: Formatting action IDs (editor.bold, editor.bulletList, etc.) and their labels are constants that define the formatting command interface and must never drift between registration and dispatch.
judgment.differences: formatBar.tsx uses these as UI button labels and dispatch targets; actions.ts registers them as action handlers with titles. The excerpt doesn't show the full action registration, but both sites reference the same action ID strings.
judgment.owner: src/editor/ (should own the canonical action ID and label definitions)
judgment.rationale: Extract formatting action IDs and labels to a shared constants module (e.g., src/editor/formatActions.ts) so both formatBar dispatch and actions registration import from one source of truth; prevents silent mismatch between UI buttons and registered handlers.

judgment.invariant: Both apply a parameterized line-level transformation to editor state, update cursor position by delta, and maintain selection/scroll state.
judgment.differences: The transformation function called (applyHeading vs applyBlockToggle) and its parameter type (level vs kind).
judgment.rationale: Identical mechanical pattern for line transformation + cursor repositioning in same file and language; extract as a generic helper to prevent cursor-positioning or selection-handling divergence.

judgment.invariant: Both implement a filterable list surface with search input and empty-state messaging.
judgment.differences: AllChatsSurface searches chats by title/slug with simple substring matching and alphabetic sorting; NoteListSurface is a generic component with debounced full-text API search, local filtering, and pinned-then-recency sorting.
judgment.rationale: The sites use a common design-system vocabulary (CSS classes, size constants) but encode independent domain logic (chat vs. note semantics, different search/sort strategies); extracting a shared component would require excessive parameterization and obscure the distinct purposes.
